hints.content:
We want to complete $x^2\blueD{+14}x$ into a perfect square.

To do that, we should add $\left(\dfrac{\blueD{+14}}{2}\right)^2=\goldD{49}$ to it:

$x^2\blueD{+14}x+\goldD{49}=(x+7)^2$

In order to keep the expression equivalent, we add and subtract $\goldD{49}$, not forgetting the expression's constant term, $64$:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=x^2+14x+64
\\\\
&=x^2+14x+\goldD{49}+64-\goldD{49}
\\\\
&=(x+7)^2+64-49
\\\\
&=(x+7)^2+15
\end{align}$

In conclusion, after completing the square, the function is written as

$f(x)=(x + 7)^2 +15$
